claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To give you an accurate answer, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you're claiming or wish to claim Child Benefit for?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 21 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I appreciate you providing Alex's details.

Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to let you know that Child Benefit typically has an age limit. Let me ask you a clarifying question:

**Is Alex still in full-time education or apprenticeship, or is he currently working or not in any of these situations?**

This information will help me determine whether he might still qualify despite being 21 years old.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education or an apprenticeship. He's not working either - he's just sort of figuring things out at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Let me read the official eligibility rules to make sure I have the correct information about age limits for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official eligibility rules I've just reviewed, I'm afraid I have some disappointing news regarding Alex.

According to the Child Benefit eligibility criteria, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if a child is **under 16**, or if they're **16 or over but under 20 and staying in approved education or training**.

Since Alex is 21 years old and is not in approved education, training, or an apprenticeship, he would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit.

**Do you have any other children that you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?** If so, please tell me their names and ages, and I can assess whether you'd be eligible for them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is my only child. So just to confirm - I'm not eligible for Child Benefit then?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's correct. Based on the eligibility rules, you would **not be eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex because:

1. Alex is 21 years old
2. He is not in approved education or training
3. Child Benefit eligibility ends at age 16 (or up to age 20 if the child is in approved education or training)

Since Alex doesn't meet these criteria, you would not qualify for Child Benefit.

However, if Alex's circumstances were to change in the future—for example, if he were to enter approved education or training before turning 20—his eligibility situation might be different. But based on his current situation, unfortunately you cannot claim Child Benefit for him.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
No, that's clear. Thank you for explaining it to me.

</invoke>
